misconceptions.description: Assuming any cut is acceptable regardless of unknown count
misconceptions.trigger: learner cuts through many unknown members and still expects a direct solution
misconceptions.feedback: In planar truss section analysis, you usually want no more than three unknown cut-member forces because the isolated section gives three independent equilibrium equations.

misconceptions.description: Choosing moment centers without considering which unknowns can be eliminated
misconceptions.trigger: learner takes moments about a point that leaves all unknown cut-member forces in the equation
misconceptions.feedback: A good moment center is chosen to eliminate as many unwanted unknowns as possible, often at the intersection of two cut-member lines of action.

misconceptions.description: Thinking the method of sections avoids solving support reactions
misconceptions.trigger: learner begins with a cut before accounting for support loads
misconceptions.feedback: Support reactions usually must be found first because they act on the cut section as external forces.
